prompt:
Add src/cachekit/ttl.py with class WeightedTTLCache(max_weight, default_ttl=None, clock=time.monotonic, on_evict=None).
- put(key, value, weight=1, ttl=<default_ttl>): weight is an int > 0; ttl is in seconds and > 0, or None for an entry that never expires. Leaving ttl out uses default_ttl; passing ttl=None explicitly means the entry never expires even when default_ttl is set. Invalid weight or ttl raises ValueError.
- An entry put at time t with ttl expires at t + ttl (clock() >= t + ttl): from then on it is gone everywhere (get, peek, in, len, weight, delete).
- An entry heavier than max_weight raises ValueError and leaves the cache unchanged, including an existing entry with the same key.
- Putting an existing key replaces its value, weight and expiry and makes it the most recently used entry.
- After a put, while the total weight of live entries exceeds max_weight, evict the least recently used live entry and call on_evict(key, value) for it.
- get(key, default=None) returns the value of a live entry and makes it most recently used; it does not change the expiry. peek(key, default=None) and `key in cache` do not change recency.
- delete(key) removes a live entry, otherwise raises KeyError. len(cache) and the property cache.weight count live entries only.
- stats() returns {"hits": ..., "misses": ..., "evictions": ...}: hits and misses count get calls only; evictions counts only entries evicted to make room (not expirations, deletes or replacements).
One test in tests/ fails; fix the bug behind it.
Add tests for the new behaviour. Run all tests with: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
